title: The Julian calendar takes effect
text: Caesar's reformed calendar begins: 365 days and a leap day every four years. Still, mostly, in production.

title: Cicero born
text: Marcus Tullius Cicero is born at Arpinum. Latin prose acquires its benchmark.

title: Caesar crosses the Rubicon (traditional date)
text: "Alea iacta est." The Republic's last civil war begins.

title: Octavian "restores the Republic"
text: He returns his powers to the Senate, which hands them straight back — plus Gaul, Spain and Syria. Three days later he is Augustus.

title: Octavian receives the title Augustus
text: The Senate grants the name; historians date the Empire from here. Version 1.0.

title: Theodosius I dies; the Empire is divided
text: Arcadius takes the East, Honorius the West. They never reunite.

title: Caligula assassinated; Claudius found behind a curtain
text: Praetorians kill Caligula and proclaim his uncle Claudius, reportedly discovered hiding in the palace.

title: Hadrian born
text: Future builder of walls, the Pantheon, and a beard trend.

title: Trajan becomes emperor
text: Nerva dies; his adopted heir, away in Germania, takes over. The Empire heads for its greatest extent.

title: Otto I crowned Holy Roman Emperor
text: Pope John XII crowns Otto in Rome; the Holy Roman Empire — a claimant, see above — is conventionally dated from here.

title: Septimius Severus dies at York
text: "Be harmonious, enrich the soldiers, scorn all others." Caracalla and Geta are not harmonious.

title: Augustus named Pater Patriae
text: The Senate grants him "Father of the Fatherland" — the title he said he valued most.

title: Constantine XI Palaiologos born
text: The last Roman emperor is born in Constantinople.

title: Heraclius dies
text: Victor over Persia, loser of Syria and Egypt, first emperor styled Basileus.

title: Lupercalia: Antony offers Caesar a diadem
text: Caesar refuses the crown three times in public. A month later it no longer matters.

title: Diocletian's first edict against the Christians
text: The Great Persecution begins at Nicomedia.

title: Hadrian adopts Antoninus Pius
text: Succession sorted — on condition that Antoninus adopts Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus in turn.

title: Edict of Thessalonica
text: Theodosius I, Gratian and Valentinian II make Nicene Christianity the state religion.

title: Constantine the Great born (traditional)
text: Born at Naissus (Niš); the year is disputed, c. 272.

title: Antoninus Pius dies; Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus co-emperors
text: The first time two Augusti rule jointly.

title: Elagabalus assassinated
text: Killed by the Praetorians along with his mother; Severus Alexander succeeds.

title: Ides of March: Caesar assassinated
text: Stabbed 23 times at the Theatre of Pompey. The soothsayer was right.

title: Tiberius dies at Misenum
text: Caligula succeeds. Rome celebrates. Rome will regret this.

title: Marcus Aurelius dies
text: The last of the "Five Good Emperors" dies on campaign; Commodus takes over. Gibbon starts the decline here.

title: Battle of Munda
text: Caesar's last battle: the Pompeian cause dies in Spain.

title: Ovid born
text: Publius Ovidius Naso, at Sulmo. Future author of the Metamorphoses; future exile.

title: Pertinax murdered; the Empire auctioned
text: The Praetorians kill Pertinax and sell the throne to Didius Julianus for 25,000 sesterces per man.

title: Battle of Thapsus
text: Caesar crushes the Optimates in Africa; Cato kills himself at Utica.

title: Caracalla assassinated
text: Killed by a soldier while relieving himself by the roadside near Carrhae. Macrinus, the praetorian prefect, is suspiciously ready.

title: Septimius Severus proclaimed emperor
text: At Carnuntum, by the Pannonian legions. He marches on Rome.

title: Zeno dies
text: The emperor who received the Western regalia in 476 dies in Constantinople; Anastasius succeeds.

title: Fourth Crusade takes Constantinople
text: The city falls on 12 April; three days of looting follow. A Latin Empire is installed.

title: Natalis Urbis: Rome founded
text: Varro's date for Romulus founding the city. Happy birthday, Rome — still celebrated on the Capitoline, with costumes and some very serious re-enactors.

title: Marcus Aurelius born
text: In Rome. The Meditations are some decades away.

title: Diocletian and Maximian abdicate
text: The only emperor to retire voluntarily goes to grow cabbages at Split. The Tetrarchy starts to fail almost immediately.

title: Constantinople dedicated
text: Constantine consecrates Nova Roma on the Bosporus. The Empire's centre of gravity moves east.

title: Constantine the Great dies
text: Near Nicomedia, after a deathbed baptism. His sons divide the Empire, then subtract each other.

title: Fall of Constantinople
text: Mehmed II's troops breach the Theodosian Walls; Constantine XI dies in the fighting. The Roman state ends after 2,206 years. This site counts from here, too.

title: Didius Julianus executed
text: After 66 days, the man who bought the Empire is killed as Severus approaches Rome. "But what evil have I done?"

title: Vandals sack Rome
text: Geiseric's fleet lands at Portus; fourteen days of methodical looting begin.

title: Battle of Antioch
text: Elagabalus's supporters defeat Macrinus; a fourteen-year-old sun priest becomes emperor.

title: Nero's suicide
text: "Qualis artifex pereo." The Julio-Claudian dynasty ends; the Year of the Four Emperors begins.

title: Leo III the Isaurian dies
text: Saviour of Constantinople in 717–718 and father of Iconoclasm.

title: Vespasian dies
text: "Vae, puto deus fio." Titus succeeds; the Colosseum opens the following year.

title: Julian dies in Persia
text: Mortally wounded near Samarra: the last pagan emperor. Jovian hands Nisibis to the Persians to get the army home.

title: Vespasian proclaimed emperor in Alexandria
text: On the Kalends of July the legions of Egypt acclaim him; Judaea and Syria follow. The Flavian dynasty begins.

title: Hadrian dies at Baiae
text: "Animula vagula blandula…" Antoninus Pius has to lobby a hostile Senate to have him deified.

title: Julius Caesar born (12 or 13 July)
text: Gaius Julius Caesar is born in the Subura. Gaul has not been warned.

title: Great Fire of Rome
text: Breaks out among the shops by the Circus Maximus and burns for six days, then reignites. Nero was at Antium.

title: Constantine proclaimed emperor at York
text: The troops at Eboracum acclaim him on his father's death. The Tetrarchy's succession plan dies the same day.

title: Byzantines retake Constantinople
text: Alexios Strategopoulos walks in through an unguarded gate; the Latin Empire ends and the Palaiologan restoration begins.

title: Octavian enters Alexandria; Antony dies
text: Antony falls on his sword; Cleopatra follows on 10 or 12 August. Egypt becomes Octavian's personal province.

title: Claudius born
text: At Lugdunum (Lyon) — the first emperor born outside Italy.

title: Battle of Cannae
text: Hannibal's double envelopment annihilates the largest army Rome had ever fielded. Rome does not negotiate.

title: Battle of Zela
text: Caesar defeats Pharnaces II in a five-day campaign. "Veni, vidi, vici."

title: Holy Roman Empire dissolved
text: Francis II abdicates under Napoleon's pressure. The longest-running claimant shuts down after 1,006 years.

title: Majorian executed
text: The last capable Western emperor is deposed and beheaded by his general Ricimer.

title: Battle of Pharsalus
text: Caesar defeats Pompey in Thessaly; Pompey flees to Egypt and is murdered on arrival.

title: Battle of Adrianople
text: The Goths destroy the Eastern army and the emperor Valens is killed. Ammianus: no battle in Roman history except Cannae was so destructive.

title: Octavian's triple triumph begins
text: Three days of triumphs for Illyricum, Actium and Egypt. The doors of the Temple of Janus are closed: peace, officially.

title: Alexios I Komnenos dies
text: The emperor who asked the West for mercenaries and got the First Crusade.

title: Trebizond surrenders
text: The last Byzantine splinter state falls to Mehmed II. Last Roman process terminated.

title: Augustus dies at Nola
text: After more than forty years as princeps. "Acta est fabula, plaudite." Tiberius succeeds.

title: Vesuvius erupts (traditional date)
text: Pompeii, Herculaneum and Stabiae are buried; Pliny the Elder dies. Some evidence points to an autumn date instead, 24 October.

title: Alaric sacks Rome
text: The Visigoths enter through the Salarian Gate. The first sack of the city in 800 years; three days of looting.

title: Battle of Manzikert
text: Romanos IV Diogenes is captured by the Seljuks; Anatolia begins to slip away.

title: Caligula born
text: Gaius Julius Caesar Germanicus, nicknamed "little boot" by his father's soldiers.

title: Commodus born
text: At Lanuvium, to Marcus Aurelius and Faustina. Future gladiator.

title: Battle of Actium
text: Octavian and Agrippa defeat Antony and Cleopatra off western Greece. The Republic's last civil war is effectively over.

title: Romulus Augustulus deposed
text: Odoacer removes the last Western emperor and sends the imperial regalia to Constantinople. Day 1 of this site's main counter.

title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest (9–11 September)
text: Arminius destroys three legions under Varus. Augustus: "Quintili Vare, legiones redde!"

title: Aurelian born
text: Future Restorer of the World, at Sirmium (probably).

title: Titus dies
text: After twenty-six months; Domitian succeeds. "I have made but one mistake."

title: Trajan born
text: At Italica in Hispania — the first emperor from the provinces.

title: Domitian assassinated
text: A court conspiracy; the Senate elects Nerva and orders damnatio memoriae. The "Five Good Emperors" begin.

title: Antoninus Pius born
text: At Lanuvium. Future quietest emperor.

title: Augustus born
text: Gaius Octavius, in Rome. His birthday later became the start of the civic year in the province of Asia.

title: First Battle of Philippi
text: Brutus beats Octavian; Antony beats Cassius, who kills himself believing all is lost. Round two on 23 October.

title: Claudius dies; Nero emperor
text: Mushrooms, allegedly. Agrippina's son, aged sixteen, takes the purple.

title: Virgil born
text: Publius Vergilius Maro, near Mantua. "Arma virumque cano" is forty years away.

title: Battle of Zama
text: Scipio Africanus defeats Hannibal; the Second Punic War ends on Rome's terms.

title: Second Battle of Philippi
text: Brutus is defeated and dies by suicide. The Republic's last army is gone.

title: Domitian born
text: In Rome: the Flavian who would be damned by memory.

title: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
text: Constantine defeats Maxentius at the Tiber under the chi-rho. In hoc signo vinces.

title: Ottoman sultanate abolished
text: The last ruler to style himself Kayser-i Rûm leaves office. Successor claims: 0 active.

title: Cicero's First Catilinarian
text: "Quo usque tandem abutere, Catilina, patientia nostra?" Catiline leaves Rome that night.

title: Nerva born
text: At Narni. Future sixteen-month emperor and adoptive father of Trajan.

title: Justinian I dies
text: The emperor who never slept finally does. Hagia Sophia, the Code, and a reconquered (and plague-ravaged) West are his legacy.

title: Tiberius born
text: Tiberius Claudius Nero, in Rome. The reluctant second emperor.

title: Vespasian born
text: At Falacrinae in the Sabine hills. The Colosseum's commissioner.

title: Diocletian proclaimed emperor
text: By the army at Nicomedia. The Crisis of the Third Century ends; the Dominate begins.

title: Cicero killed
text: Proscribed by the Second Triumvirate; his head and hands were displayed on the Rostra.

title: Horace born
text: Quintus Horatius Flaccus, at Venusia. "Carpe diem" pending.

title: Belisarius enters Rome
text: The Eastern Empire retakes the old capital from the Goths. Rome is, briefly, Roman again — the closest this site has ever come to a YES.

title: Julian enters Constantinople
text: Sole emperor after the death of Constantius II; the pagan restoration begins.

title: Nero born
text: At Antium, as Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus; renamed on adoption by Claudius.

title: Basil II dies
text: The Bulgar-slayer dies with a full treasury and no heir. Peak Byzantium begins its descent.

title: Saturnalia
text: Io Saturnalia! Gifts, role reversal, gambling, and a public banquet — the festival reorganised in 217 BC that a later holiday quietly absorbed.

title: Charlemagne crowned "Emperor of the Romans"
text: Pope Leo III crowns him in St Peter's. Constantinople files an objection that takes twelve years to settle.

title: Aurelian dedicates the temple of Sol Invictus (traditional)
text: The Unconquered Sun gets a temple and a festival, the Dies Natalis Solis Invicti. Draw your own conclusions about 25 December.

title: Commodus assassinated
text: Strangled in his bath by the wrestler Narcissus on the last day of the year. Gladiator got the revenge plot wrong and the vibe right.
